# Breadcrumb

Universal element component for navigation breadcrumbs. / /* `items` defaults to `[]` even though its prop type is `isRequired`. A required prop is a lint, not a guarantee: React renders anyway, and `items.map` on `undefined` took the whole page down rather than the one breadcrumb. Found by `DocumentedContract.stories.jsx`, and only once this component's page gained a Usage tab: the guard renders each DOCUMENTED prop against fabricated required props, and it cannot fabricate an `arrayOf(shape)`. So documenting `separator` is what first rendered a Breadcrumb with no items, and the crash had been reachable by any caller all along.

Also asked as: path, navigation trail.

## Usage

Use `Breadcrumb` when a page sits inside a hierarchy the user needs to see and
climb — a student inside a cohort inside a program, a lesson inside a unit. It
answers two questions at once: where am I, and what is one level up. When the
hierarchy is one level deep, a single "Back to X" `Link` says the same thing
with less furniture.

It takes a single `items` array of parents, ordered root first. Each item is
`{ text, href, onClick }` and renders as a link. The current record is not an
item: the `PageHeader` title names it.

## Motion

Breadcrumb reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Drill into and climb back out | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Arrives with its page, one level longer; its row opens from its seam once, at Drill depth 1. |
| exit | Drill into and climb back out | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Leaves with its page. |

## Alternatives

- For progress through a sequence of steps, use `ProgressTracker`.
- For moving between sibling views of the same subject, use `Tabs`.
- For a persistent hierarchy the user browses rather than retraces, use `Sidebar`.

## Best practices

### List parents only. {#list-parents-only}

```jsx
// Incorrect — the last item is the current record. The page title already
// names it, so the trail repeats it.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />

// Correct — every item is a parent the person can climb to.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
]} />
```

### Pass `href` alongside `onClick` on ancestor items. {#pass-href-alongside-onclick-on-ancestor-items}

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no href the item renders as a plain list item, not a link,
// and its onClick is never attached: nothing happens on click.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026', href: '/cohorts/a26' },
]} />

// Correct — the href makes it a real, focusable link; onClick intercepts it
// for the router. The component calls preventDefault for you.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026', href: '/cohorts/a26' },
]} />
```

### Pass a string to `separator`, not a node. {#pass-a-string-to-separator-not-a-node}

Despite the `node` prop type, the value is written into the breadcrumb's
divider custom property, and a custom property holds text. A string is quoted
for you and works; a React element is stringified by CSS and disappears. Pass
`'/'`, `'›'`, `'—'`.

Do: A string separator is quoted for you.
Don't: A React element is stringified by CSS and disappears.

### Show the whole path, root first. {#show-the-whole-path-root-first}

A trail that starts mid-hierarchy leaves people unsure where they are. List every parent from the top down to the page's own parent, and let a level too long end in an ellipsis rather than dropping it. A trail of five or more levels folds its middle levels into the menu, never drops them.

Do: Every parent from the root down.
Don't: The trail starts mid-hierarchy, so the top is missing.

### Keep the trail on one line and truncate each level. {#keep-the-trail-on-one-line-and-truncate-each-level}

A level longer than its room ends in an ellipsis with its full text in a Tooltip while clipped; the trail never wraps. Five or more levels fold the middle into a "…" button named "Show hidden levels", which opens the hidden levels as links, in order; the root and the last two stay. See [Overflow](?path=/docs/patterns-states-overflow--docs).

### Use it for position, not for history. {#use-it-for-position-not-for-history}

A breadcrumb shows where a page sits in the hierarchy, never the pages the person happened to visit. The trail for a page is the same whichever way they arrived.

### Name each level literally. {#name-each-level-literally}

Use the page's own title, not a direction or a pointer.

Do: Short, literal names that match the page titles.
Don't: Names that mean nothing out of context.

## Accessibility

- **The landmark is handled.** It renders a `nav` around an `ol`, one link per
  parent. The current record is the page's heading, not a crumb, so no item
  carries `aria-current`.
- **Every breadcrumb is named "breadcrumb" unless you say otherwise.** Pass
  `label` to name the landmark when more than one breadcrumb appears on a page.
- **Keep `text` short and literal.** It is the whole accessible name of the
  link. "Autumn 2026" navigates; "here" does not.
- **The separator is generated content.** It is a `::before` on each item after
  the first, not text in the list; the `ol` structure is what states the
  nesting.
- **`id` lands on the last item.** Not on the `nav`. If you need to point an
  `aria-describedby` or a test at the trail as a whole, use `className`.

## Related

- `PageHeader`: use when placing `Breadcrumb` in the page header's `breadcrumbs` slot above the page title.
- `Link`: use when rendering a single "Back to X" link for a one-level return.

Same group: `Link` · `Pagination` · `Sidebar` · `Tabs`

## Parts

1. **Landmark and list.** A `nav` named by `label` around an ordered list, one item per level, root first.
2. **Parent link.** Every item, in the link color; an `onClick` intercepts it for a router.
3. **Separator.** A slash drawn between items; `separator` swaps the character.
4. **Fold.** On a trail of five or more levels, the middle levels fold into a "…" icon button named "Show hidden levels", which opens them as a menu; the root and the last two parents stay visible.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Parents in the link color with no underline. |
| Hovered | Underline on an ancestor link; the ink stays the link color. |
| Pressed | No change of its own. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring on the link for keyboard focus; see Border. |
| Disabled | Not a state. A level the person cannot open is left out, never a dimmed link. |

| Row | `--control-md`, `--body-default` |
| Gap and separator space | `--stack-md` |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each level as the page is titled, in sentence case. | Abbreviate or invent a shorter name that appears nowhere else. |
| Keep each name to a few words so the trail fits on one line. | Repeat the full page title when it runs long. |
| List parents only; the page title names the current record. | Add the current record, a trailing arrow or the word “current”. |
| Use real nouns: “Autumn 2026”, “Lessons”. | Use “here”, “back” or “click”. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | The parents, root first, as `{ text, href, onClick }`. List parents only: the current record is not a crumb, the page title names it. An item without `href` is plain text, not a link. `onClick` replaces the navigation with a handler. Five or more items fold all but the first and last two behind a "…" menu named "Show hidden levels". |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the last item. |
| `separator` | node | `'/'` | What is drawn between items. A string is used as is; the default is `/`. |
| `label` | string | `'breadcrumb'` | Accessible label for the nav region that wraps the breadcrumbs. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the `nav` element beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the `nav` element. |
